rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies tribo-corrosion under sliding contact, but uses a different HEA composition, chloride electrolyte, and wear-only/corrosion-only baselines rather than thermally shocked AlCoCrFeNi2.1 compared directly with DS2205.
rationale.condition_agreement: It identifies sliding in a corrosive environment over ambient-to-elevated temperatures, but omits the specified thermal-shock treatment, deionized water, temperature points, loads, frequencies, stroke, timing, and alumina counter-body, while introducing chloride conditions outside the target regime.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: It captures the central competition between wear-induced depassivation and passive-film repair, but misses the temperature-dependent transition among abrasion, stable polishing tribo-layer behavior, and oxide-patch disruption, as well as the stabilizing L12/B2 lamellar microstructure and DS2205 phase redistribution.
rationale.outcome_agreement: It generally predicts that passivation can make an HEA outperform conventional alloys, but does not predict the matched DS2205 comparison, the order-of-magnitude wear reduction, lower friction, thermal-shock phase retention, or the degradation minimum near 50 °C.
